assumptions: A is a real m-by-n matrix and DeltaA(u) is a real m-by-n perturbation family indexed by unit roundoff u.
The paper constant c6 is a positive natural number and lambda is positive.
Every scalar column remainder is O(u^2) as positive u tends to zero.
Eventually on the physical domain 0 < u < 1, all columns simultaneously satisfy equation (4.17) with the exact coefficient c6*lambda*sqrt(n)*gammaTilde_m(lambda,u).

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p06_t1_columnwise_to_frobenius {m n : Nat} (A : Fin m -> Fin n -> Real) (DeltaA : Real -> Fin m -> Fin n -> Real) (columnRemainder : Fin n -> Real -> Real) (c6 : Nat) (lambda : Real) ... : exists normwiseRemainder, p06SecondOrderAtZeroRight normwiseRemainder and eventually ||DeltaA(u)||_F <= p06QRLeadingCoefficient c6 lambda m n u * ||A||_F + |normwiseRemainder(u)|
formal_statement.plain_language: If every backward-error column satisfies (4.17) simultaneously with its own O(u^2) remainder, then the whole perturbation satisfies the Frobenius-norm bound (4.20) with the same leading coefficient and one O(u^2) remainder.

informal_proof: View the column Euclidean norms as a finite Euclidean vector. Pointwise monotonicity applies the simultaneous column bounds, the Euclidean triangle inequality separates the leading and remainder vectors, and homogeneity identifies the leading vector norm with the same coefficient times ||A||_F. Bound the remainder vector's Euclidean norm by the sum of its absolute entries. That finite sum is O(u^2) because every column remainder is O(u^2).
informal_statement: The sentence preceding equation (4.20): the simultaneous columnwise backward-error bounds (4.17) imply the Frobenius-norm bound (4.20), including the additive O(u^2) term.
